own_solution.law: Snell's law gives sin(theta)=sin(40 degrees)/1.8. Side reflections preserve the magnitude of the axial velocity, so t=nL/(c cos(theta)). For L=2 m, theta=20.923 degrees and t=1.284706e-8 s.
assumptions: Geometrical optics applies, with specular side reflections.
The nondispersive glass gives pulse speed c/1.8.
An inline extension forms a continuous optical path through the same glass.
Changes stated to apply to an earlier run only do not persist into the current run.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T97AD and TACC7 replace the specified extension of 1.3 m with an unquantified 'short length', so the extension variants fail the required preservation of number and unit.

notes: The base physics and all individual numerical targets are well-posed. The invalid verdict concerns the required quantitative matching between variants. Current rod extensions give L=3.3 m and increase the time by a factor of 1.65. The separate cable and changes confined to earlier runs have no physical path to the current transit time. Diameter changes the reflection spacing and number of reflections, but cancels from total path length L/cos(theta). The two diameter sentences preserve 2.5 cm; specifying circular cross-section is consistent with the ordinary reading of diameter.
